title: Man dies in RCMP custody; A 24-year-old Langley man is the latest in-custody death.
article: What exactly killed a Langley man who got "erratic" on a Coast Mountain Bus in Newton last Friday remains a mystery.
The man got into a scuffle with two security guards and later died in Surrey Memorial Hospital.
The RCMP Integrated Homicide Investigation Team is awaiting a pathology and toxicology report on the cause of 24-year-old Ryan Alexander Wagemans' death.
Police say Wagemans became "erratic" on a bus that was leaving the Newton bus loop at 72nd Avenue near King George Highway. The bus driver stopped and called security for help.
The RCMP was called to assist, and Wagemans went into "medical distress."

Cpl. Dale Carr, spokesman for IHIT, said it's hoped "that through speaking to witnesses, combined with pathology results, that we will be in a position to offer a rationale for Ryan's behaviour leading up to his intervention with police and his subsequent medical condition."
IHIT is interested in speaking with anyone with any information about the man's actions on the bus or during his exchange with police at the Newton bus exchange.

Investigators have learned that Wagemans may have been on an earlier bus (the 321) before getting off and entering the 319 in Newton. They are asking anyone who was on either of those buses and has information to give them a call.
Police want to establish Wagemans's movements before 6 p.m. on June 27.
